# OpenPdfEdit

> A PDF editor that runs on your own machine. Annotate, edit text, redact, fill and sign forms, reorganise pages, OCR scans and compare drafts — documents are never uploaded, because there is nowhere to upload them to.

OpenPdfEdit is free and open source (MIT or Apache-2.0), with a Rust core
and PDFium for rendering. It ships as a native app for macOS and Windows,
a web app that runs entirely in the browser tab, and a Chrome extension —
all built from one codebase.

## What is true about it

- **Nothing is uploaded.** The desktop binary contains no HTTP client at
  all — not disabled, not opt-out, absent. The web app does the work in
  the page rather than on a server. The source is public and the claim is
  checkable.
- **No account is needed** to install it, use it, or save a file.
- **No watermark on your output, no page limit, no export cap.**
- **No analytics, telemetry or crash reporting.**
- **No AI features.** There are none in the product.
- **Free**, except two tools: watermarking and OCR are unlocked together
  for a single one-time payment of 1,000 credits. Everything else is free.

## What it does

Read and navigate (tiled rendering, find-in-document across line wraps,
bookmarks, thumbnails, tabs, undo/redo). Annotate (highlight, underline,
strikeout, sticky notes, freehand ink, shapes, comment list, XFDF import
and export, flatten). Edit content (replace a line of text in place, move
text runs, move images, true redaction). Organise pages (reorder, rotate,
delete, insert, split, merge, crop, page numbers). Forms and signing (fill
fields, add fields, draw and place signatures). Protect and finish
(password encryption, compression, watermark). Read scans and compare
drafts (OCR in twelve languages, text and pixel comparison between two
documents).

## Things people get wrong about it

- **Redaction is real content removal**, not a black rectangle drawn over
  live text. The words are removed from the page's content stream —
  including text inside form XObjects — the covered pixels of an image are
  overwritten, and the file is rewritten rather than appended to, so
  nothing survives in an earlier revision. The box drawn on top is a
  second line of defence, not the mechanism.
- **OCR runs locally.** The recogniser and its language data are served
  from this site's own origin and run in the browser or on the desktop;
  the scan is not sent anywhere.
- **The web app works offline** after its first load, including across a
  reload.
- **Editing text does not reflow the page.** A PDF stores positioned
  glyphs rather than paragraphs, so a replaced line does not push the
  lines around it. When the original font is not embedded, the substitute
  is named rather than swapped in silently.
